q-50028.name: Question 1
q-50028.problem: A fly’s position relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by the function $x(t)=\frac{t}{2}-\frac{\pi }{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}t)\,\text{m},$ where $t$ is the time in minutes. Find its average position of the fly between $0$ and $2$ minutes.
q-50028.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the position on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{x}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}\,{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{2-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{t}{2}-\frac{\pi }{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}t))\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{{t}^{2}}{4}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}t))|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((\frac{{2}^{2}}{4}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}\cdot 2))-(\frac{{0}^{2}}{4}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}\cdot 0))) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}((1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(0+1)) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average position is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\,\text{m}.$

q-50028.html:
Question 1
?

A fly’s position relative to a fixed origin O is given by the function x(t)=t2−π8sin⁡(π8t)m, where t is the time in minutes. Find its average position of the fly between 0 and 2 minutes.

a
24m
b
2m
c
22m
d
2−22m
e
28m
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To calculate the average value of the position on [t1,t2], we use the average value formula xavg=1t2−t1∫t1t2x(t)dt.

So, we get

xavg=12−0∫02(t2−π8sin⁡(π8t))dt=12(t24+cos⁡(π8t))|02=12((224+cos⁡(π8⋅2))−(024+cos⁡(π8⋅0)))=12((1+22)−(0+1))=24.

Therefore, the average position is 24m.

q-83246.name: Question 2
q-83246.problem: A golden eagle is moving in a straight line with a velocity of $v(t)=\frac{{2}^{t}}{12}\,\text{m/s},$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. Find the average velocity of the golden eagle on the interval $[2,6].$
q-83246.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the velocity on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{v}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}v(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{6-2}\,{\int }_{2}^{6}(\frac{{2}^{t}}{12})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 12\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2}({2}^{t}){|}_{2}^{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{48\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({2}^{6}-{2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{60}{48\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{5}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average velocity is $\frac{5}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,\text{m/s}.$

q-83246.html:
Question 2
?

A golden eagle is moving in a straight line with a velocity of v(t)=2t12m/s, where t is the time in seconds. Find the average velocity of the golden eagle on the interval [2,6].

a
54m/s
b
58m/s
c
52ln⁡2m/s
d
54ln⁡2m/s
e
58ln⁡2m/s
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To calculate the average value of the velocity on [t1,t2], we use the average value formula vavg=1t2−t1∫t1t2v(t)dt.

So, we get

vavg=16−2∫26(2t12)dt=14⋅12⋅ln⁡2(2t)|26=148ln⁡2(26−22)=6048ln⁡2=54ln⁡2.

Therefore, the average velocity is 54ln⁡2m/s.

q-83252.name: Question 3
q-83252.problem: Find the average acceleration of a particle on the interval $[0,2]$ if its acceleration in ${\text{mm/s}}^{2}$ is given by the function $a(t)={e}^{t}+2t,$ where $t$ is the time in seconds.
q-83252.worked_solution:
To calculate the average value of the acceleration on $[{t}_{1},{t}_{2}],$ we use the average value formula

$$
{a}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{{t}_{2}-{t}_{1}}\,{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}a(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{2-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{t}+2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{t}+{t}^{2}){|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[({e}^{2}+{2}^{2})-({e}^{0}+{0}^{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{2}+4-1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average acceleration is $\frac{1}{2}({e}^{2}+3)\,{\text{mm/s}}^{2}.$

q-83252.html:
Question 3
?

Find the average acceleration of a particle on the interval [0,2] if its acceleration in mm/s2 is given by the function a(t)=et+2t, where t is the time in seconds.

a
(2e+3)mm/s2
b
12(e2−1)mm/s2
c
(e2+4)mm/s2
d
12(e2+3)mm/s2
e
14(e2+1)mm/s2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To calculate the average value of the acceleration on [t1,t2], we use the average value formula aavg=1t2−t1∫t1t2a(t)dt.

So, we get

aavg=12−0∫02(et+2t)dt=12(et+t2)|02=12[(e2+22)−(e0+02)]=12(e2+4−1)=12(e2+3).

Therefore, the average acceleration is 12(e2+3)mm/s2.

q-353941.name: Question 4
q-353941.problem:
A robotic sled moves along a straight track with velocity 
$v(t)={t}^{3}-t,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds and $v$ is measured in meters per second.

Find the average acceleration ${a}_{\text{avg}}$ over the time interval $t\in [1,3].$ Do not round your answer.

${a}_{\text{avg}}=$ 
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$
q-353941.worked_solution:
The average acceleration is the average rate of change of the velocity, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{v(b)-v(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{v(3)-v(1)}{3-1} \\  & =\frac{[(3)^{3}-(3)]-[(1)^{3}-(1)]}{2} \\  & =\frac{(27-3)-(1-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{24-0}{2} \\  & =\frac{24}{2} \\  & =12\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average acceleration is $12\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

q-353947.name: Question 5
q-353947.problem:
A test cart moves in a straight line with velocity 
$v(t)=\frac{3}{t},$ where $t$ is measured in seconds and $v$ is measured in feet per second.

Find the average acceleration ${a}_{\text{avg}}$ over the time interval $t\in [1,3].$ Do not round your answer.

${a}_{\text{avg}}=$ 
{{field-1}}
${\text{ft/s}}^{2}$
q-353947.worked_solution:
The average acceleration is the average rate of change of the velocity, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{v(3)-v(1)}{3-1} \\  & =\frac{[\frac{3}{3}]-[\frac{3}{1}]}{2} \\  & =\frac{1-3}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2}{2} \\  & =-1\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average acceleration is $-1\,{\text{ft/s}}^{2}.$
